### Transducer
A **transducer** is an electronic device that converts a physical quantity (such as temperature, pressure, light, or displacement) into a proportional electrical signal (voltage, current, or resistance), or vice versa.

---

### Difference Between Active and Passive Transducers

| Feature | Active Transducer | Passive Transducer |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **External Power Source** | Does not require an external power source (self-generating). | Requires an external DC or AC power source to operate. |
| **Working Principle** | Operates on energy conversion principles (e.g., piezoelectric effect, thermoelectric effect). | Operates on the variation of passive electrical parameters (resistance, capacitance, inductance). |
| **Examples** | Thermocouple, Piezoelectric crystal, Photovoltaic cell. | Resistance Temperature Detector (RTD), LVDT, Thermistor, Strain gauge. |
proTip: Remember that active transducers are 'self-generating' and do not need external voltage/current sources.
